# Conditional probability

**Definition:** P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B), provided P(B) > 0.

$$P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$$

## Independent events

A and B are independent (indep) if and only if $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$.

- Mutually exclusive is NOT the same as independent!
- If P(A) > 0 and P(B) > 0, mutually exclusive (mut excl) events can't be independent.

## Bayes' rule

$$P(B \mid A) = \frac{P(A \mid B)P(B)}{P(A)}$$

Example: a test for a disease with sensitivity (sens) 0.95, specificity (spec) 0.9, and prevalence 0.01 gives P(D | +) ≈ 0.088.
